description: Changes the SPEED of a train of silence-separated events without changing the events: inter-onset intervals are divided by factor (silence edited in or out), event content untouched. Verified: factor 2 moved onsets 0.05/0.70/1.30/2.00 to 0.05/0.375/0.675/1.025 (intervals exactly halved); factor 0.5 doubled them. Real duration = lead + (last_onset - first_onset)/factor + last_event_len - data-dependent, so the static model is the flat-material baseline (on no-silence material the mode WARNS 'only 1 event found' and near-passes-through, 1.9999773 s from 2.0 - the duration row rides that path). Event detection = runs of >= minsil ms of EXACT digital zeros (no threshold exists). factor is the family's only BREAKPOINT-CAPABLE parameter (banner: 'can vary over time'; verified: a 0.5->2 ramp renders 2.057 s, distinct from both scalar endpoints) - accelerando/rallentando of the event train. Deterministic; stereo accepted.
musical_use: Tempo-change without timestretch artifacts: double-time a drum phrase or speech rhythm while every hit keeps its exact original timbre and length - only the air between events moves. factor > 1 compresses the rhythm (up to audibly frantic before events start touching), factor < 1 relaxes it into spacious slow-motion where each event hangs in silence. The breakpoint form is the star: ramp factor 0.5 -> 2 for a phrase that starts dragging and ends rushing (a written-out accelerando cut from the real performance), or spike it briefly for a stumble. -s/-e confine the speed-change to a time window (verified live) so you can rush only the middle of a phrase; -a picks which event stays anchored in place. Needs true digital silence between events - gate first, or hand-time with retime 1/6/7.

factor.description: Speed-change factor for the event rhythm: inter-onset intervals are divided by it (2 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half speed). CDP-enforced '(0.010000 to 100.000000)'; factor 1 refused 'ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: No change in tempo.' BREAKPOINT-CAPABLE (verified: 0.5->2 ramp differs from both scalar-endpoint renders; banner 'can vary over time'). Time axis = input time.

minsil.description: Minimum run of EXACT-ZERO samples that separates events (CDP-enforced '(0.045351 to 10000.000000)' at 44.1 kHz, srate-dependent floor). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 2 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.').

start.description: Time at which speed changing begins (CDP-enforced 0 to the input duration - refusal quotes '(0.000000 to 2.500000)' on a 2.5 s file; Parameter[3]). Verified live with -e (render and duration change).

end.description: Time at which speed changing ends (runtime-bounded by the input duration). Events outside [start, end] keep their original spacing.

sync.description: Approximate time of the infile event that stays synchronised with its copy in the output (banner: time must be WITHIN the event; 0 = sync at first event). Verified live (changes both render and duration).

examples.expected_use: Inter-onset gaps halved, events untouched; 2.5 s 4-event fixture renders 1.445 s.

examples.description: Written-out accelerando: drag to rush over the phrase.
examples.expected_use: Event spacing starts stretched, ends compressed (verified distinct from both constant-factor renders).

known_issues: EVENT DETECTION = EXACT ZEROS (no threshold; source ibuf[i]==0.0). No-silence material does not refuse: 'WARNING: WARNING: only 1 event found: Change inter-event silence ??' + near-passthrough (one frame short, residual <= 3.5e-4) - this baseline IS the static duration model.

REAL duration on event material: lead + (last_onset - first_onset)/factor + last_event_len (verified exact at factor 2/0.5 on two fixtures). Small factors expand hugely (factor 0.01 -> ~100x the event span) - the static pre-flight under-predicts; the engine watchdog/duration cap is the guard.
factor 1 is refused ('No change in tempo.') - for a no-op just copy the file.
Deterministic (identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart); stereo accepted (1.4450 s 2-ch matches mono).
